newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ming Kee to buy 71.3 pct of Sharp Brave.
newsitem.headline: Ming Kee to buy 71.3 pct of Sharp Brave.

text.p: Ming Kee Investments Ltd, a private firm owned by businessman Simon Chan, said it has agreed to buy a 71.30 percent stake in Sharp Brave Holdings Ltd from it parent Leung Kee Holdings Ltd for HK$73.28 million.
The deal would be carried out in two tranches with the completion of the frist tranche of 259.99 million shares around February 10, the firms said in a statement on Tuesday.
The price represented about HK$0.203 per Sharp Brave share and Ming Kee would make a general offer for all outstanding shares at the same price after the completion of the first tranche, they said.

Leung Kee said the sales of the second tranche of 101 million shares or 19.95 percent was expected to be completed on or before the last business day in the six month period from the date of the first completion.
Ming Kee, the vehicle created by Chan to carry out the purchase, said it has no intention to make any material change to the existing business of the Sharp Brvae group.
It was also the firm's intention to maintain the listing of Sharp Brave shares on the Hong Kong stock exchange.
Sharp Brave engages in investment holding, manufacturing and trading of electronic products.
Chan is chairman of Billion Finance Co, which specialises in offering finance to small enterprises, and will become executive chairman of Sharp Brave.
Trading in shares of Leung Kee and Sharp Brave resumed on Tuesday after being suspended since December 24.
Sharp Brave was up HK$0.04 at HK$0.28, while Leung Kee was up 0.009 at HK$0.225.
